narrative_text: An employee had been using tubing tongs to tighten loose bolts on a hanger bracket. As the employee was setting the tongs down, they triggered while the employee's fingers were between the tong clamps. The employee suffered an amputation to the right middle fingertip, as well as crushing injuries to the index and ring fingers.

An employee was grinding at a pedestal grinder on a small piece of work. The work had been set in place using vice grips. The work slipped from its placement, moving and lodging into the space between the work rest and the disc. The employee's left hand was also moved by the force into this area, lacerating/crushing his index, middle, and ring fingers.

An oil derrick operator was reaching out to remove slack in a cable. His right hand was caught between the cable and the rod elevator as the rig operator came down with the blocks. His ring finger was crushed and his middle finger was amputated.
An employee was operating a mini jerk machine when his hand was smashed between the lever and the machine.

An employee was monitoring a mud pump and slipped on a slick surface. While bracing for a fall, the employee contacted a belt and pulley on a pump. His right middle finger was lacerated just above the first knuckle and the fingertip had to be surgically amputated.

An employee was removing a thread protector off the end of an alloy when the alloy shifted and pinched their finger between it and the catwalk. The employee sustained an open fracture of the left index finger and a fingertip amputation.
An employee was operating a preform press when his hand was caught in the machine, resulting in a left index finger amputation.
An employee was cleaning a roller with a rag when the rag became caught in the roller. The employee's right index finger was pulled into the roller, causing an abrasion and requiring hospitalization.

An employee working on an oil-and-gas service rig suffered partial amputations of the right middle and right ring fingers after his hand was caught between the tong plate and the pin that secures the tongs.
An employee pulled on a winch line, causing a horse head to slide down and strike the employee's right foot, fracturing it.

An employee was attempting to break loose a pipe connection with a pipe wrench when his thumb was caught between the pipe and the wrench when the pipe string was lifted. He suffered a soft tissue amputation to the tip of the thumb.
An employee was crawling under a truck/trailer to service the water pump PTO when his arm was caught in the rotating PTO driveline, severing his right forearm and requiring hospitalization.

An employee was working to install a drive belt on a water pump. He was holding the belt on both sides of the pulley, working to route it over the top. As he pulled down with his right hand, the pulley rotated and the belt slid over it, pulling his left little finger between the pulley and the belt. He suffered an amputation to the fingertip as well as a fracture to the ring finger.
While performing pump maintenance an employee's right hand was caught in the pump area and crushed.

An employee was reinstalling wiring on a lowboy trailer. The door on the hydraulic compartment was open. Strong winds from a storm blew the hydraulic compartment door shut and the employee's right hand was caught in the door resulting in amputation of the middle fingertip.

On April 27, 2018, at approximately 7:00 AM, an employee was operating a drill and had just finished drilling two holes in some square tubing when he attempted to grab a shaving near the drill bit, which caught his glove. His left thumb was then pulled into the drill bit, severely cutting it and resulting in a partial amputation.

An employee and coworkers were attempting to change out a leaking O-ring. They were using a 3-ton come-a-long to create a gap when the hook on the come-a-long broke, causing the gap to close and smash the employee's right and left thumbs.
An employee suffered a partial amputation injury when his fingers were caught in a pinch point between the hoist line and sheave.

On March 6, 2019, an employee was assisting in rigging up. He was working from about 10 feet high when he slipped and fell, his face striking the beam he was standing on. He suffered a facial injury and was hospitalized. Fall protection was being worn at the time of the incident.
An employee was walking back to the trailer after conducting maintenance outside when he slipped on ice and fell to the ground, fracturing his left hip.

Two employees were hospitalized due to injuries sustained during maintenance operations on a workover rig in the maintenance shop. One employee suffered a crushing injury when a derrick floor fell on his chest, breaking ribs and causing a collapsed lung.  A second employee suffered a broken elbow due to a fall sustained while attempting to hold the falling rig floor.

Employees were hanging a horse head on a well. The injured employee was on a pumping unit, waiting for the horse head to be lifted with rig blocks, with a safety retractable line attached. The line got caught in the blocks and pulled the employee off of the pumping unit, causing the employee to fall 10 to 15 feet before the safety line engaged. At the point of engagement, the safety line snapped, and the employee fell to the ground.
While being cut, a 20-inch metal pipe separated and a section struck an employee's lower right leg, causing broken bones.
An employee was walking through the lobby of the building when she fell on the left side of her hip and broke it. She was hospitalized and had surgery.
An employee fell from an drilling derrick while in the process of disassembling the unit.  The employee suffered injuries to the head, face and right leg as a result of the fall.
An employee was working approximately 6 feet above ground level servicing a pumpjack when he lost his footing and fell to the ground, fracturing three ribs.
While pulling a drilling pipe, the pipe broke and the jack fell onto the employee's foot crushing the steel toe portion into his foot.

An employee was measuring the produced water depth using a gauge line. After measuring, the employee began climbing down the storage tank ladder and fell. As he fell, his boots became caught between the ladder rungs, causing a right femur and left hip fracture.

An employee was doing repair work on an oil/gas well. While the rods were being spaced out, the elevator caught the bottom of the horse's head and knocked it off. It hit the ground and rolled over on top of the employee, who was working on the floor. The employee suffered a broken pelvis and a broken right femur and was hospitalized.

An employee had ascended a ladder to stand on the diesel tank of the frac pump to change the transmission oil filters. When stepping down from the ladder, he slipped and fell to the ground breaking four to ten left-side ribs.
An employee was working on a drilling rig floor. A piece of ice that had frozen to the drilling mast melted and fell off, landing on the employee's back and breaking three vertebrae.
An employee was working to assemble a rotator head onto a landing joint. The rotator head fell onto the employee's leg and fractured it.
While exiting the doghouse of a nitrogen unit, an employee fell from a ladder to the ground, suffering a back injury.

An employee was reaching between a blowout preventer (BOP) and tubing slips to pick up the BOP ring gasket when the chain broke on the BOP, causing the BOP to fall and crush the employee's right index finger. The employee's finger was amputated to the first knuckle.

A drill pipe fell. Its joint struck an employee on the right side of the hard hat, then hit his right shoulder. The employee lost consciousness and suffered a laceration to the head and shoulder, fractures to the spine, and a broken shoulder blade.
An employee was working on equipment when it fell and struck his foot causing a fracture. The employee was hospitalized.

An employee was spotting as a storage tank was offloaded from a truck to the ground. The winch cable caught on a post; the post then broke loose and was thrown into the air, striking the employee's head.
An employee was using a drilling machine when a 6-inch collar fell and struck the machine, causing it to rotate and strike the employee's left leg. The employee's left femur fractured.

An employee was disconnecting a winch truck's load line from a load when the winch truck rolled forward, tightening the line. The employee's right hand was caught by the hook and chain of the load line and the index fingertip was amputated below the fingernail.

An employee was using a pressure washer to wash a drilling rig when the washer hose became twisted. As the employee was untwisting it, the pressure washer ran over his boots, causing hot water to burn his foot and debris to enter his left middle toe. He required surgery to remove the debris.

An employee was pressure washing a piece of drilling equipment when he slightly slipped, lost his balance, and ran the tip of the pressure washer wand across his foot, causing an injection wound. He was hospitalized with a foot laceration from the high-pressure water.
An employee was spotting for a backhoe when its track struck the employee. The employee's left leg was amputated from the knee down.
An employee was changing the fuel filter on an all-terrain skid loader. The skid loader was turned on while the gear was engaged, causing the unit to roll over and crush the employee's legs.
An employee was using a pipe wrench to loosen a collar on a drilling tube. The pipe wrench broke loose and pinched the employee's right ring finger against the ground. The fingertip was amputated.
An employee was removing a pressurized choker valve at a wellsite when it separated and struck their head, resulting in a fractured jaw, fractured nose canal, and broken teeth.

An employee was blowing off pressure on a field natural gas compressor when a pipe about 3 feet long pulled out of the threads and hit the employee, causing blunt force trauma to the face, arm, and shoulder.
An employee was under a truck checking its brakes. The truck was moved and struck him, breaking and lacerating his right leg.

An employee was working on a rig floor. A casing basket fell into the tongs of a nearby rig, and the tongs would not release. Both retaining chains to the tongs released and the tong movement lever activated. The tongs swung and hit an employee, pinning him between the tongs and a derrick mast. He suffered one broken rib and one bruised lung.
An employee was operating a torque wrench to tighten equipment when his right index finger got caught in a pinch point of the tool, resulting in a partial amputation without fracture.

An employee at a remote Marathon Oil jobsite was pressure testing pipe when he was struck-by 9500psi of water when bolts broke on the flange connecting two pipes causing the high pressure water to strike the employee and one other sub-contractor's employee who were standing approximately 15 feet away.
An employee was cutting banding around a steel pipe when the pipe rolled off the rack and struck the employee's right leg, fracturing the tibia and fibula.
An employee was collecting sweeps when he opened a gut line that was pressurized and the elbow failed, dislodging and hitting his back. He suffered the loss of his spleen and a collapsed lung.
An employee was draining a plug catcher when the valve arm became loose, spun closed, and hit his right leg, fracturing it. He was hospitalized.

An employee had removed a side panel on a boom truck to diagnose an overheating issue. The belt caught his glove and pulled his left hand in, resulting in a partial amputation of his left index finger.
An employee was struck on his left leg by a high-powered pressure washer and sustained a deep laceration.

An employee was using a hydraulic torque wrench to tighten bolts on a flange. The employee's left hand was near the head where the hydraulic hose connects to the wrench. The hose became punctured and injected the employee's left-hand palm with hydraulic fluid, lacerating it.
An employee was troubleshooting a compressor when a fire occurred, burning his hands. He was hospitalized.

An employee was delivering a load to a customer location. As the employee made a right-hand turn onto a road, the tractor trailer tracked off the roadway and overturned. The employee sustained bleeding on the brain, a fractured collarbone, and a fractured finger.

A ship's crew was moving a ship along a dock. One of the ship's lines broke and struck an employee who was walking on the dock. The employee suffered an arm amputation below the elbow, a broken pelvis, and abdominal injuries.
An employee was servicing a compression unit. When he began to shut the unit down, a flash fire occurred. He suffered primarily first- and second-degree burns. He was hospitalized.
An employee was working on the engine of a compressor when a flash fire occurred, burning the employee's hands and face. He was hospitalized.

An employee was using an oxygen acetylene torch when its flame went out. He turned off the oxygen supply to the torch. The flame then returned and the torch's hose separated, causing a large flame that caused second-degree burns to his arms and abdomen. He was hospitalized.
An employee was heating oil with a hot oiler on frac tanks when a fire started. The employee was hospitalized with second degree burns on the face, hands, and back.
An employee was changing a condensate filter. A fire erupted, burning the employee's arms, legs, neck, and face.

SPN Well Services employees were inspecting gas production unit chokes for sand washing. They had inspected three units and were bleeding off pressure on a fourth when a flash fire engulfed it in flames. One of the employees suffered first-, second-, and third-degree burns.
An employee was conducting maintenance on a gas processing unit when a flash fire occurred. The employee was burned and was hospitalized. See also 1151988.
An employee was test-driving a go-cart he had been working on when it struck a parked car. He broke his left ankle and two ribs on the left side.

Three employees were servicing and cleaning an oil well when a fire occurred. All three employees were burned. One employee was treated and released. Two employees were hospitalized and one hospitalized employee required surgery.

Employee 1 was operating a crane to move a pumping unit. Employee 2 was holding a tag line. The crane lifted the pumping unit and began rotating clockwise to place it on top of a concrete base. The front driver s side outrigger and float began to sink into the ground, causing the crane to lean over. This caused the pumping unit to swing and strike into an adjacent wellhead, breaking some piping and causing a fire. The crane then fell over and it's boom broke piping on a second wellhead, contributing further to the fire. Employee 1 fell out of the cab and crawled out of the fire. He sustained burns to his face and hands and had fractured ribs. He was hospitalized. Employee 2 was burned on his cheek, arm, and leg.
An employee opened the gasoline cap to a utility trailer's generator when a flash fire occurred, causing first and second degree burns to the employee's face and hands.
An employee was injured during a  filter change when the filter caught fire. The employee was hospitalized with first and second degree burns to the hands, neck and face.

An employee was driving an ATV when it ran over a fallen tree branch. The branch popped up and went through the ATV's floor, striking the employee. The employee suffered a broken arm, a bleeding spleen and liver, and a head laceration.

While working on a saltwater disposal system, an employee was checking the rotation of a pump and noticed the oil tank was bulging at the bottom. The employee ran to get away from it when a flash fire erupted. The employee sustained second degree burns to the face, lower back, and both hands.
An employee was hydro testing and pressurizing a pipe when it blew. The lid struck the employee, causing a gash to his elbow and injury to his abdominal area that required surgery.

Employee was injured while performing a "cold cut" on a 6" metal pipe of a gathering system. Employee was burned on the face, both arms, and knees. Employee was using a striker from the welding equipment and possibly ignited natural gas.

On 11/17/2018, at 4:00 AM, an employee was working in an enclosed trailer at a customer's location, preparing down-hole tools using a break wash chemical. He was in close proximity to a space heater that ignited the fumes from the chemical. This caused second degree burns to the employee's face, requiring hospitalization.

An employee was attempting to bleed off pressure on a casing into a cellar so they could work on the casing at a drilling pad. Gas started to leak, resulting in a flash fire. The employee suffered burns to the face, ears, and hands that required hospitalization.

An employee was in the back of a truck, adding gasoline to a compressor. Some gas escaped and the fumes caused a flash fire. The employee suffered burns to the left hand, wrist, and elbow, as well as a small area on the left lower back.

An employee was working in the MCC room of the natural gas-fired gas lift compressor when an explosion occurred. It is believed that the variable frequency drive ignited the hydrates in the instrument air compressor/piping causing an explosion. The employee sustained a concussion, four broken ribs, a punctured lung and burns.

On 2/20/2016, at around 4:00 p.m., an employee was using a machine called a planner to prep the poly pipe for welding repairs when a short burst of flame occurred. The employee received second degree burns to the side of the face and neck and was hospitalized overnight.

A five-man crew had been subcontracted by Laredo Petroleum to replace the fire tubes on a heater treater and clean the inside of the tank. Three employees with Dorado Construction Group were contracted as a roustabout crew to clean the tank and replace the fire tubes, one employee of Mulholland Energy Services was contracted to operate the vacuum truck and remove the sludge from the tank, and one employee of Permian Service Co., LLC  was hired to operate a hot oil truck to provide water to the roustabout crew for cleaning. At approximately 1:00 p.m. the employees had completed pulling out the old fire tube and had begun the process of cleaning the inside of the tank from the open hatch when an explosion occurred. Three employees were hospitalized for second and third degree burns to their arms and face.

An employee was manually lighting burner boxes on hot oil trucks. When using a cigarette lighter to ignite a pilot burner a liquid propane gas flashback (woof) occurred and the employee suffered flash fire burns to the face and lungs.
An employee was using a safety can to fuel a 4" trash pump with gasoline. The fuel ignited and the employee sustained burns to their arms and hands.

An employee working in the maintenance garage was conducting an oil change on a vehicle and was looking for a drum to collect the oil.  The employee and another employee found a partially full drum that was labeled as methanol.  The employees thought the drum potentially contained water.  They took the drum outside and poured some of the contents on the ground.  The employee that was conducting the oil change applied a lighter to the material on the ground.  The material caught on fire.  As the other employee was attempting to move the drum out of the area, some of the liquid exited the drum, and was ignited by the fire on the ground.  The employee that was conducting the oil change suffered second degree burns to his right leg from the knee to the ankle.
An employee was working on trucks when his shop rag ignited from a spark, causing his clothing to catch on fire. He sustained burns on his arms and legs and was hospitalized.

Two employees were unloading and loading propane cylinders. A leaking propane tank was placed in front of a makeshift structure. Propane gas accumulated within the structure and an explosion occurred. Both employees suffered second and third degree burns that required hospitalization.

An employee was cleaning a sight glass on a gas separation machine that was located on top of a self contained/self evacuating tank. When the valve that connected the well bore to the gas separation machine was opened, gas/vapor ignited, causing a flash fire that burned the employee's face and hands.

An employee was draining condensate from an air compressor when a catastrophic failure occurred on a check valve on a natural gas line. The natural gas began blowing toward the running compressor and the gas ignited causing an explosion. The employee was hospitalized for second and third degree burns to the face, hands, left leg, and left midsection.

An employee was operating a front-end loader to push flowback solids into the solids bay when fumes from a liquid were ignited causing a flash fire and burning the employee's face and the backside of a hand.

An employee was welding an oil pipe and installing a gauge on the pipe of a drilling rig. As he cut into it with a torch, an explosion occurred. The shockwave of the explosion caused the employee to sustain a concussion and multiple broken bones.

An employee was opening the valve of a separator tank to drain the tank when a flash fire occurred and burned the employee's hands, face, and head. The employee was wearing fire-resistant clothing at the time of the incident.

An employee was troubleshooting the hydraulic system on a customer's skid to get the hydraulic pump to run. He started up the engine and an unexpected release of hydraulic energy occurred. He attempted to open the dump valve and the discharge hose exploded with his hand on it, releasing oil and severely lacerating his right index finger.

An employee was lining up a water injection pump when naphtha and hydrogen sulfide were released. The employee was exposed and was hospitalized for injuries to the lungs. Personal protective equipment was not being worn at the time of the incident.

Frac technicians conducting monitoring operations on water levels of gauging tanks during oil and gas drilling operations are potentially overexposed to air contaminants and respiratory irritants such as chlorine, hydrogen sulfide, and benzene.  Recently, an employee was admitted to the hospital for observation and treatment after suffering from an extreme coughing episode after working a monitoring shift at the worksite.  A second employee was treated and released.
An employee was unloading a truck tank when he was exposed to hydrogen sulfide, suffering a headache and nausea.
An employee was hospitalized for hydrogen sulfide exposure while pulling tank bottoms at an oil and gas waste disposal site.
On July 17, 2925, an employee was working on a computer inside a vehicle when they began experiencing symptoms of carbon monoxide poisoning, resulting in hospitalization.
An employee who was troubleshooting a level transmitter was found unconscious within the vicinity of a suspected hydrocarbon (H2S) release.
An employee's H2S monitor went off while he was delivering salt water on location. He eventually became ill and was hospitalized with respiratory problems.
An employee was performing tank gauging on a produced water tank. After opening the tank's thief hatch, the employee was exposed to hydrogen sulfide, suffering headaches and nausea.

An employee was preparing to shoot a fluid level on a well. He screwed an echo gun onto the well casing and opened the casing valve. When the pressure hit the gun, the outside of the casing valve threads failed and the pressure popped, releasing H2S (hydrogen sulfide) gas into the employee's face.
An employee was exposed to hydrogen sulfide and was hospitalized for an inhalation injury.
An employee was found unresponsive inside of a trailer with a running generator. He was hospitalized for carbon monoxide exposure.
An employee opened the hatch on an oil tank. The exposure to hydrogen sulfide and other gases caused the employee to become ill, dizzy, and lightheaded; the employee was hospitalized.

A three-person crew was unloading pipe. Two crew members were outside of the truck handling the pipe on the rack. They loaded the three joints of pipe and moved to load the polish rod. One end of the rod was stuck into the ground so they picked up the opposite end and stood the 22' rod into the air to lay it down. The rod contacted a live, overhead electrical line and the two employees were electrocuted. Both employees also sustained electrical burns.

While performing a break-out and disassembling equipment on-site, an employee removed the meter cover. Then, while removing the bypass blades with pliers and a screwdriver, the screwdriver contacted the meter box, causing an arc flash. The employee sustained second degree burns on his face, chest, and left hand, and sustained a second/third degree burn on his right hand.
An employee was moving a panel switch to the open position on a 480-volt motor control center breaker when an electrical arc flash occurred, burning the employee's eyes, face, neck, and hands.
An employee was working at a shaker table to properly dispose of oil and gas drilling waste when a water pump created an arc flash that burned the employee's face.
An employee received an electric shock with the wrench cable the employee was holding made contact with the power line.
An employee was measuring the voltage of an electrical transformer following a new installation when an arc flash occurred. The employee sustained burns to both right and left hands and fingers.
An employee was unwiring the secondary side of a de-energized transformer and draining oil for repairs when a wire came loose and shocked the employee. The employee was hospitalized.

Employee's were vacuuming a rig and were going to pull a pump. The injured employee raised the mast and it struck a power line. The employee sustained electrical burns to their right hand, right and left forearms, and feet.
An employee was holding several of an oil drilling rig's electrical cables while the rig was being transferred from one well to another. The cables were damaged, and the employee was shocked.

An employee was checking control voltage in an electrical panel when an electrical short occurred, causing an arc flash which resulted in third-degree burns on the hands and second-degree burns on the face of the employee.
An employee was troubleshooting an electrical cabinet when there was an arc flash, which burned his right hand and face.
An employee was hospitalized after sustaining an electrical shock while unscrewing a light bulb on a training rig.
An employee was working on the controller drive for the down hole equipment when he received an electrical shock, resulting in burns to the right thumb and left forearm and face.
An employee was exposed to an arc flash while conducting an electrical switching procedure on an electrical panel in the tank farm. His left shoulder and hand were injured.

On March 15, at 11 a.m., an employee was running a cable to the floor of a pulling unit when the employee was shocked by approximately 1,050 volts DC from the trailer truck. The employee was hospitalized with an electrical shock to the hands.
On April 23, 2019, an employee was testing the voltage on a 34.5-kV, 4160/2400 step-down transformer when an arc flash burned the upper right part of his body. He was hospitalized.
An employee was cleaning the head of a hot roller when their glove got caught in the roller, pulling their arm into it and resulting in burns to their forearm.

An employee was driving through a construction zone after unloading production water at a disposal well when his vehicle veered off the road and crashed south of Killdeer, North Dakota, on Highway 22. He suffered back injuries.

An employee was working outside on July 17, 2018, preparing for the next day's job when he started not feeling well. The next day, July 18, 2018, the employee was at a customer location working and started vomiting and was unable to keep any fluids down. The employee was hospitalized for heat exhaustion and renal failure.

On or about 1300 hrs on 31 May 2015, a One Source Industrial Services employee was hospitalized when the employee's vehicle overturned on CR 5000 in Andrews County, Texas. The incident occurred as the employee attempted to turn onto CR 5000. The employee lost control of the vehicle, causing it to overturn and resulting in a broken arm, bruised ribs, and a possible concussion.
An employee was servicing a gas lifting system when the system released pressure and struck the employee. The employee sustained injuries that required hospitalization.

While conducting maintenance on top of a double cone process, an employee stepped on a valve that released >200 degrees of fluid. The fluid contacted the employee, causing burns to the shoulder, abdomen, and torso.

While assisting a coworker, an employee was cracking a suction line to determine if hot asphalt was unloading from a truck when they were sprayed with the 460 degree hot asphalt. The employee sustained second degree burns to the left side of their nose, cheek, ear lobe, chin, and part of their neck.
An employee was cleaning the inside of a tanker truck and passed out, requiring hospitalization.

An employee was transferring hot roofing tar (350 degrees Fahrenheit) from the truck to the tank when the hose connection to the truck came off, spraying them with hot tar. This resulted in burns to both hands and arms from the elbows down and on the right side of their head, including their ear.

A dump truck was trying to avoid rocks on a trail when its left-side wheels left the trail. The truck rolled about three times, and the driver suffered a neck strain, bumps and bruises, a laceration to the forehead that required stitches, and a laceration to the right forearm.

An employee was repairing a trash pump used to treat water for drilling and fracking. The trash pump vapor locked and the employee was trying to get the pump started when the hose ruptured and they were exposed to a 12.5% bleach solution. The employee sustained chemical burns to their arm and leg.
An employee was tying a hose. A truck backed up, pinching the employee's leg between the hose and hammer union, resulting in a right fibula fracture.

At approximately 8:20 AM, a hose on the discharge line on a dehydrator unhooked and triethylene glycol sprayed the owner and two technicians. The chemical was approximately 300+ degrees. Another technician manually closed the valve. One employee was treated for second-degree burns to the left arm and left calf and was released. The employee who was closest to the unit was sprayed on the left arm, wrist, and leg, and sustained third-degree burns. He was hospitalized.
An employee's fingers were pinched in tongs, resulting in an amputation.
An employee was walking in his working area when he slipped on mud and fell, injuring his leg.
Employee was injured when he fell 20-40 feet from an elevated man-lift.
An employee was hooking up a hose when the hose fell and crushed their fingertip.
An employee was bitten on the right calf by a spider while working at a drilling rig.
An employee was struck by falling blocks from a crane.
An employee slipped on a step and fell forward injuring both knees.
The driver of an asphalt truck hit the overpass of a bridge.
An employee sustained an amputation to his left ring finger while working on a drilling rig.
An employee was struck on the left side by a cable coming from the cable drive while drilling.
An employee was unloading pipe racks when a rack fell on and broke the employee's leg.
An employee was walking around equipment, tripped over hydraulic lines and fell to the ground. The employee sustained a broken hip.
An employee was walking around the back of his truck when he slipped on ice and fell to the ground, breaking a hip.
An employee exited a building, tripped over a plastic sign (9" x 12") on the ground, and fell. The employee was hospitalized due to a fractured left tibia and fibula.
An employee fell on a ramp, sustaining a broken leg.

An employee was walking across the rig floor carrying a large bolt, called a connecting pin, when he tripped on an object and fell to the floor. The bolt impacted the end of his left ring finger and amputated the fingertip.

An employee was walking from a front office to a mailbox located outside when the employee slipped and fell to the floor at the front door. The employee was hospitalized and had surgery for a fractured right hip.

A cement crew had finished a surface cement job and was preparing to rig down the cement head and equipment. An employee was preparing to remove the cementing head and manifold from the casing. The drilling rig crew loosened the chain boomer and lifted the casing to remove the slips. When the rig operator lifted the casing, the hook on the chain boomer broke, striking the employee in the hard hat and knocking him to the rig floor. He hit his head on the floor, losing consciousness and suffering a head laceration.
An employee was filling a refrigerator with bottled water when the employee slipped and fell on the concrete floor. The employee was hospitalized with a fractured right hip that required surgery.
An employee fell while standing on a crescent wrench, cutting his leg on a valve.
At 10:00 p.m., on June 19, 2019, an employee was helping a coworker line up a flange prior to bolt-up when he lost his footing and fell to the ground, fracturing his femur. He was hospitalized.
An employee's left little finger was pinched between a wrench and a forklift bucket, resulting in an amputation.

An employee was preparing an oven for charging and cracked the seal of the jump lid to release pressure. Flames unexpectedly released from the oven and burned the employee's right ring and little fingers. The employee sustained second-degree burns.

Employees were flushing a chemical line at a job site. As an employee was unplugging a hose connection, residual pressure caused caustic liquids to spray under his face shield, resulting in chemical burns to the face and neck that required hospitalization.

An employee was disconnecting a braided metal flex hose that was supplying air to a furnace for the de-coking process. A supplier sent an alternate feed to the furnace, which required the furnace to remain online. The employee went to disconnect the flex hose from the furnace and received second degree burns to the face and first degree burns to the torso from steam/hot condensate. The line was not depressurized at the time of the incident.
An employee was testing a pipe at an oil/well site. The pipe moved and caught his finger, causing the amputation of the fingertip.
On May 2, 2024, an employee was dumping a hopper into a bigger dumpster when his left ring finger got caught by the hopper and was amputated.
An employee was pressure washing pipes when the fitting on the spray wand broke and the hot water contacted the employee, resulting in burns to his stomach and thighs.
An employee had been attaching barricade tape when their right foot was fractured by a crane's outrigger.

An employee was working to replace an air line. The line needed to be trimmed to fit and the employee was using a utility knife to cut the hose. The knife cut through the hose and the employee's glove, amputating their left index fingertip.
An employee was performing well maintenance activities when equipment failed and a rope socket struck the employee's face and chest. They suffered facial injuries.
A team of employees was carrying a 10-foot section of iron tubing. One of them slipped and the tubing struck the back of his head. He suffered dizziness and blurred vision.
An employee was removing a pipe with a 36" pipe wrench. The employee was backing up when he slipped and fell backwards hitting his head on a rack.
An employee was standing on a trailer adjusting its load. A piece of equipment shifted, causing the employee to fall to the ground and strike his head. He suffered head trauma.

An employee was on the tubing platform of a production rig placing tubes in the elevators when his safety line became snagged by the tubing being elevated. The employee was lifted off of the platform until his line separated, then he fell onto the platform. The employee sustained back and neck injuries and five broken ribs. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee fell from a ladder and fractured an arm and a leg.
An employee was hospitalized due to heat exhaustion.

An employee tripped and fell to the ground.  The employee landed on his knees in a pile of hot petroleum coke.  The employee sustained burns on both legs from the coke, and possibly the hot steam.  The employee was taken by ambulance to Christiana Hospital, and later transferred to Crozer-Chester Medical Center in Chester, Pennsylvania.  The employee sustained 2nd degree burns on his legs, and 3rd degree burns on his ankles.
An employee was removing nuts from a pump unit. The employee slipped and their right index fingertip was crushed between the pump and a rachet. The fingertip was amputated.

An employee was tripping production pipe in a well using a rig and traveling block. A pipe slipped in the well, causing a pressure change and blowout. The employee went down an escape line and fell at about 10 feet above the ground, fracturing and lacerating his face.

An employee was on a ladder accessing the top of a vessel. He was using a hand wrench to tighten an outlet piping flange. The wrench slipped off the flange, causing the employee to fall 8 feet to the ground and sustain 4 rib and 3 back fractures. Fall protection was not worn at the time.
The employee was conducting a pressure test of a Blow Out Preventer (BOP) when a high pressure water spray contacted the employee's right armpit causing a 1/4 to 1/2" laceration.
Two employees were burned when a bubble tower exploded creating a flash fire during maintenance work on a well site.
While pulling drilling rods, a driller did not stop and hit the crown of a derrick block. The rods then hit a derrickman, breaking his pelvis.

Employees were opening a hatch at one of the salt water disposal tanks when a spark created a flash fire. The employee was burned in the flash fire and hospitalized. The other employees received minor skin burns and were examined and released the same day.

An employee was removing an elevator bell when the winch line caught slack, causing the bell to fall and crush the employee's right hand. The employee's right ring and middle fingertips were amputated.

A crew was working to remove tubing from a well. A 2-inch hose was connected to the tubing for fluid circulation. The crew was raising the tube when the hose was caught and came under tension. An employee attempted to dislodge the hose, which reacted and sprung into the employee's face, breaking bones. The employee was hospitalized.
An explosion occurred while an employee was performing work on a well head. He sustained burns to 60% to 80% of his body.

An employee was taking a butane gas sample as part of the hydrocarbon refining process. A component disconnected and the butane ignited, resulting in first- and second-degree burns to the employee's forearms and to their face, including their cheeks, chin, and neck.

An employee had been conducting crane operations. The employee went to stop a piece of oil and gas equipment for tubular running from falling over to the ground. Their right hand was caught between a rolling ladder and the equipment, resulting in fractures to the index and middle fingers. They were hospitalized and the middle finger required surgery.
An employee was using a pneumatic wrench to tighten a clamp when their thumb became pinched in the clamp, resulting in amputation of the thumb tip.

An employee was completing a rig down and had finished cementing. He was attempting to remove the cement plug of the plug container by lowering the plug to the ground using a wench. The plug shifted and the employee's left wrist was caught between the drill pipe and the manifold on the plug container. The employee was hospitalized with a dislocated left wrist.
An employee's middle finger was caught between two road guardrails that were being stacked. The employee suffered a partial amputation to the finger.

An employee was assisting with installation of a pipe cutting machine. During the installation, the machine slipped off the pipe. The employee attempted to grab it and their right little finger was pinched between the machine and the ground, resulting in a partial amputation of the fingertip.

An employee was power washing the top shed of the shakers approximately 8 feet above the lower level. As he was transferring to the ladder to leave the shed top, he fell and struck his head on the tank's metal grating. The employee suffered a torn muscle in the neck and a concussion.
An employee cut into a hollow rod that was filled with fluid pressure, which caused a bar to flip and hit the employee's left arm. The employee's forearm was broken.

An employee was working on the rig floor while setting a casing when the employee lost balance and placed the left hand on the casing. At the same time, the casing slips were released and the inter-tool slid down, amputating the employee's left index finger at the first knuckle.
An employee slipped and twisted his right ankle while attempting to carry a 50-pound bag of seed, fracturing his fibula and tibia.

An employee was approximately 1 foot high on an uneven surface, removing the cross-over pin from a casing collar, when the employee slipped on the uneven surface and fell to the ground. The employee fractured the first four vertebrae.

An employee had just replaced a rubber O-ring on a manifold and was trying to put the bull plug back on the missile when it slipped off and took the employee's hand down, striking it against the flat metal plate below. As a result, the employee suffered a partial fingertip amputation.

An employee was standing on the rig floor watching another employee operate a set of power tugs when the tugs slipped and rotated, hitting the employee. The employee was knocked from the rig floor and struck the ground. The employee suffered a fractured lower right leg and right wrist.

While conducting well-servicing operations, an employee was setting up the work floor of a workover rig. The employee slipped on loose dirt, causing him to lose his grip on the wing portion of the rig floor. The wing portion fell, landing on his left ring finger and amputating the fingertip.
An employee was walking in the company kitchen when she slipped on water and fell to the floor, resulting in a broken hip.

An employee was cutting 3/4-inch strips of wood with a table saw when a piece of scrap wood became stuck between the guard and the saw blade. As the employee attempted to remove it, the left index fingertip contacted the blade and was partially amputated.

An employee was about to go down a flight of stairs but noticed someone coming up the same stairs. He then re-directed to go to another set of stairs but tripped and fell. He shattered his left elbow and was hospitalized.

An employee was performing rigging operations at a well pad. He was walking on a containment pad walkway that was slippery from a recent rain/snow event. He slipped and fell. He attempted to catch himself during the fall and fractured his left wrist. He was hospitalized.
While climbing into construction equipment, an employee slipped and fell onto an operating handle, suffering a broken left rib and punctured lung.
An employee slipped on water droplets on the floor and fell, breaking her left hip and right ankle.
An employee was exiting a truck when he lost his footing while descending the cab stairs. He fell to the ground and injured his left elbow, requiring hospitalization.

A workover crew was tripping out of a hole when the drill line parted, causing the blocks to drop from 10 to 15 feet up and fall onto the floor. The drill floor sprung up when the blocks contacted it, throwing an employee off the floor. He fell approximately 15 feet onto the ground, breaking a rib.
An employee was operating a pulling unit on a rig when he tripped on a pipe, fell,  and broke his leg.

An employee was performing maintenance on the frac pump and was using a pry bar to roll the pump for re-packing. The pry bar slipped and struck the employee's head. He then fell striking his head on the ground and sustained a concussion.
On or about August 31, 2016, an employee was disconnecting drill pipe joints in the rig and slipped and fell. The drill pipe joint came down and struck his right hand middle and index fingers.

Two employees were carrying a drill bit and installation tool to the center of a drilling rig floor. One of them slipped and fell, and the drill bit and installation tool landed on his left hand. He suffered an open fracture and partial amputation of the last joint of the little finger, as well as a laceration to the ring finger.
An employee was checking around a work area. The employee tripped on a ground rod that was sticking up about 2 inches from the ground and suffered a broken left knee.
An employee slipped and fell on ice in the parking lot. He injured his knee and required surgery.

The injured employee was overseeing that the rod connections were going well. A work crew was coming out of the well with 1.5-inch, fiberglass rods and double stands. They had just made the connection. An approximately 60-foot fiberglass rod unscrewed from the holding, slipped out of the transfer, fell out of the barrack, and hit the rig floor. It then bounced off the rig floor onto the ground and struck the injured employee on the left side of the head, knocking him unconscious.
Employees were pulling slips while running drill pipe in a well bore. An employee suffered a hernia.
An employee was slipping pipe when it became stuck and the pipe snapped, striking the employee in the back and ribs. The employee sustained fractured ribs.
An employee tripped and fell while walking across a rig floor, suffering multiple fractures to the left elbow.
An employee was rigging up a swab lubricator when he tripped on an uneven surface and broke his tibia and dislocated the fibula.

An employee was installing a rear suspension airbag beneath a hydro-excavation truck when the airbag slipped off the truck's frame and struck him in the face. The employee sustained multiple facial fractures and an intraparenchymal hemorrhage and was hospitalized.

An employee was working on the rig floor and tripped over an object that he just placed on the rig floor falling to the ground. The employee landed on his shoulder fracturing an arm and dislocating his elbow.

An employee was changing the belts on a pumping unit. The employee left one bolt in place and held the 40-pound guard up with his shoulder. The guard slipped from his shoulder and lacerated his bicep, requiring hospitalization.

Two employees were installing plastic on a strainer basket inside of a reactor 30' high when the basket slipped and pulled in one employee's glove and middle finger. Approximately 1/4" of the employee's left middle fingertip was amputated. The basket is made of steel and is shaped like a small garbage can measuring 2' x 1.5' and weighing 200 pounds.
An employee was walking to his truck when he slipped in the mud and hit his head and back, suffering a concussion and spinal fracture.
An employee was lacing up the line with paper when he lost his balance and fell to the floor, breaking his foot and ankle. He required surgery.
An employee was walking back to the work area, slipped, and fell to the ground fracturing the right tibia and fibula.
An employee was detaching a 200-pound bale at or near an oil well site. He tripped on a rock and fell backward and the bale fell on his abdomen, causing internal bleeding.

An employee was clearing ice on top of a drilling rig doghouse landing. Hinges broke when the employee jumped to clear the ice, and the employee fell to the ground 20-plus feet below. The employee suffered fractures to the lumbar region, wrist, and ankle.
The employee was walking, tripped over a wooden pallet, and fell breaking his hip.
An employee was using a ratchet wrench to tighten a bolt when the wrench slipped, catching his finger between it and a piece of steel. His left-hand third fingertip was amputated.

An employee was holding/monitoring the purging "pigging" of a concrete pumping hose after testing. The hose began flailing and struck the employee in the face, causing face, jaw, cheek, and nose injuries/lacerations. The employee was hospitalized.

An employee was changing out a bolt on the kicker (moveable object) on the driller side of the PDS (stationary object) control box on the rig floor. The kicker came down on his right hand, catching it between the kicker and the trough. The employee sustained fractures to his thumb and index finger, as well as lacerations to the top and bottom of his hand.
A discharge hose failed, striking an employee and causing a laceration and fracture of the right tibia. The employee was hospitalized.
A flowback operator was cutting a hole in a 55-gallon poly drum. The knife closed on his left little finger, cutting it. He was hospitalized; the finger was amputated.

An employee was performing abrasive blasting on two six-inch pipes. While rolling the pipe in the kneeling position, the blast nozzle engaged. They sustained an abrasion of the right inner thigh from the abrasive blasting media contacting them at 95 PSI.
An employee was performing maintenance on equipment while pressuring the unit up to the correct PSI. His hand was on top of the equipment when the air punctured his hand.

An employee was working with a crew on the rig floor tripping pipe into the hole. They applied the manual tongs as and the line that supplied air to the clutch froze. When the driller started the draw works forward, the rotary turned unexpectedly. One of the snub lines, which anchor the tongs in place, was secured to the rig but not to the tongs. The tongs turned and struck the worker in the chest and the employee sustained collapsed lungs, a bruised liver and kidneys, a damaged spleen, and broken ribs.

An employee was standing on the floor plate of a drilling rig when the method of attaching the floor plate to the structure failed. The employee fell 17 feet to the ground, suffering a head laceration that required surgery.
An employee was cleaning wet sand from the sand bin gate when the gate closed on his left hand, causing multiple fractures and lacerations. He required sutures.

Two employees were attempting to clear a clog from a cellar with a water hose. As they moved the hose into the cellar, an obstruction came out and pushed the hose out.  The hose whipped around, striking both employees in the face, causing lacerations and facial bone fractures.
An employee was assisting in hydroblasting operations and received a laceration to the left calf when the water cutting machine malfunctioned.

An employee was walking on the beam portion of the pumping unit attempting to guide the "horse's head" into position when the "horses-head" moved unexpectedly and struck the employee's right foot resulting in a fracture and laceration to the foot.

An employee was operating power tongs and running casing into a hole. The CRT tool fell 40 feet from the top drive striking the casing stump and the employee. The employee suffered four amputated toes on their right foot and a puncture wound on their back and was hospitalized.

An employee was checking the air trap and noticed some shell cuttings were clogging up the trap. He was walking around to wash them out when he walked through some steam and did not see the step down. He fell onto the metal grated floor, landing on his left hip and left knee. The employee was hospitalized and required hip surgery.

An employee was walking alongside a burned-out truck that was being moved into a yard by a tow truck. The employee's right foot passed in front of the driver's side tire rim, and the tire ran over the employee's steel-toed footwear. The employee suffered a lacerated little toe, a broken middle toe, and another laceration.

An employee was holding a pup joint when a catwalk pushed the joint forward, causing it to strike their upper body. The employee suffered four broken ribs, internal bleeding from the pancreas, and bruises to their stomach and chest.
An employee was cutting fabric with a knife when the knife stabbed the employee's leg.

An employee was disassembling a wire-line tool when a section of the tooling fell onto the employee's hand. The employee sustained deep lacerations to four fingers and small fractures to two fingers, requiring hospitalization.

An employee was lowering a well pump down a well shaft when a 1/2-inch cable snapped and whipped back up, striking the employee. He suffered lacerations to both hands and bruising on the chest, requiring hospitalization.
An employee was helping to unstring a drill line when the drill line became hung up in the fast line. The drill line then came free, striking and lacerating the employee's right thigh.

An employee was standing on the rig floor when a chain broke while cement was being piped into the casing. The broken chain struck the employee on the hard hat resulting in a laceration and a possible eye socket fracture.

On or about 4/29/15, an employee's index finger on right hand was amputated while cutting a 2 x 6 wood slab on a table saw. The employee was hospitalized. The employee's 4th and 5th digits on the right hand were repaired as well.
An employee was restarting a compressor when he bumped into the side of a staircase and suffered a bruised leg. The employee was hospitalized.

An employee was swapping out sides of a choke manifold during drill out operations when the threaded end of a 10K needle valve parted from the end cap and struck the employee causing a laceration to the right leg.
An employee was hydroblasting the tubes in a spare condenser with a lance. As he moved the lance from one tube to the next, the lance engaged, jumped back, and lacerated the employee's right hand.

An employee was on top of a haul truck trailer, taking tiedowns for a pumping unit's crank guard to be lifted with a crank. The employee fell approximately 5 feet off the trailer and landed on one foot, resulting in fractures to the tibia and fibula, which caused a muscle injury. The employee was hospitalized and had surgery.

On April 19, 2019, at approximately 9:00 a.m., an employee was breaking down pipe with a sledge hammer when he threw out his back and experienced lower back pain. He was hospitalized with a herniated disk at the L4 and L5 vertebrae.
An employee tripped and twisted his ankle while stepping down from a machine. He suffered a displaced fracture to the right fibula and a sprained ligament in the right ankle.
An employee was walking the floor when a fork truck backed up and struck the employee resulting in foot fractures and a sprained knee.

On May 24, 2017, at approximately 9:00 p.m., an employee was attempting to isolate a pump and needed to clean the strainer basket. After opening the system, the employee was hit with steam, suffering second degree burns and requiring hospitalization.

While an employee descended a wooden stair case, a stair tread began to give way. The employee shifted his weight to the handrail and the handrail gave way, causing the employee to fall approximately two feet to the ground. The employee landed on his back, then slid down the hill and contacted a concrete barrier. The employee was hospitalized with lower back pain.
An employee was cleaning a clogged strainer on a pump. Upon removal of the strainer, stored up steam was released and burned the employee's face, chest and right arm.

An employee opened an access panel on a pipe rattler unit to adjust the pipe by hand. His right hand made contact with the pipe cleaning brush, which was still energized at the time, rubbing the skin on his hand away to the muscle layer.
An employee was retrieving a dust cap from an asphalt auger when his right ring fingertip was amputated. The employee was hospitalized.

At the facility shop area, an employee tripped over his feet and fell on an industrial sized valve stem used in hydrofracking (a piece of sharp equipment) and lacerated his abdomen.  This injury required hospitalization for two days.

An employee was driving a powered industrial truck  when it struck a pillar. The employee was ejected and his head came into contact with the structure of the truck. He suffered a head injury and was hospitalized, requiring surgery.
